Ph-negative disease (atypical CML) carries a worse prognosis, and some classification sys- tems consider it to be a separate disease.1-3 CML occurs in 3 different phases. It is usually diagnosed in the chronic phase, which may last for several years, which when untreated, progresses to an advanced phase; this consists of an often rapidly fatal blastic phase (blast crisis), which is often preceded by a transition period, the accelerated phase.1,3-7 The development of imatinib, an inhibitor of the BCR- ABL protein tyrosine kinase, constituted a revolutionary change in the management of CML.1-5,8,9 The Internation- al Randomized Study of Interferon and STI571 (IRIS), found imatinib to be better than interferon alfa with low- dose cytarabine for newly diagnosed CML in chronic phase.10,11 Follow-up study found responses to be durable in a high proportion of patients.12 The optimal dose has not been determined, and high-dose imatinib is under investi- gation.4,8 However, since relapse is common after stop- ping imatinib, therapy should be continued indefinitely in responsive patients.1,8 Resistance may also be a prob- lem.2,3,5,7-9,13-15 For patients who do not respond to initial therapy with imatinib, or are in haematological relapse, options include increasing the dose of imatinib, the use of second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as dasat- inib or nilotinib, considering allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), or investigational thera- py.1,3,6,7 For patients unable to tolerate imatinib or other ty- rosine kinase inhibitors, interferon alfa (with or without low-dose cytarabine) or hydroxycarbamide may be rea- sonable alternatives.1,2,4,8 Early allogeneic HSCT (p.1811) has the potential to cure CML due to a graft-versus-leukaemia effect, but it is still associated with appreciable morbidity and mortality, in- cluding graft-versus-host disease,9 and results with imat- inib have challenged the role of HSCT as first-line therapy for chronic phase CML.1 While HSCT is still an option in suitable patients such as younger patients with HLA-iden- tical sibling donors,4,5 or those with high-risk disease and low transplantation risk,2 most recommend an initial peri- od of therapy with imatinib since the response can either reinforce or weaken the indication for HSCT.6,8,9
